# AVB Basics
AVB (Audio Video Bridging) is an extension to the Ethernet standard designed to provide guaranteed quality of service, which simply means that audio samples will reach their destinations on time. 

AVB networking offers several features that make it ideal for audio applications:

- Low, predictable latency. AVB provides latency of no longer than 2 ms sending an audio stream point-to-point over up to seven “hops” (trips through switches or other devices) on a 100 Mbps network. With higher speed networks, many AVB devices support lower latencies and additional hops. 

- Scalable, with high channel counts. AVB’s bandwidth is sufficient to carry hundreds of real-time channels using a single Ethernet cable. This offers the future possibility of expanding your system with additional devices that contain different kinds of audio I/O, multiple controllers, and other useful functions.

- Guaranteed bandwidth. AVB networks intelligently manage the data traffic giving priority to AVB data. This means standard network traffic, such as Internet streaming, won’t prevent your audio from being delivered reliably and on time.

- Integrated clock signal. In a digital audio system with multiple devices, having a master clock is critical to maintaining audio fidelity. The AVB specification defines such a clock to be accurately distributed to all devices in the system.

On the simplest level, AVB works by reserving a portion of the available Ethernet bandwidth for its own traffic. Because packets of AVB data are sent regularly in allocated slots within the reserved bandwidth, there are no interruptions or interference, making AVB extremely reliable.

What makes AVB ideal for audio networking is that it splits network traffic into real-time traffic and everything else. All real-time traffic is transmitted on an 8 kHz pulse. Anything that’s not real-time traffic is then transmitted around that pulse. Every 125 µs, all real-time streams send their data. Other packets are transmitted when there is no more real-time data ready to be transmitted. To make sure that there is enough bandwidth available for all prioritized real-time traffic, the Stream Reservation Protocol (SRP, IEEE 802.1Qat) is used.

Every AVB compliant switch between each talker and listener will then make sure sufficient bandwidth is available using SRP, making it a foundational building block of the AVB standard. Every switch and AVB device on the network must implement SRP and send real-time traffic at the 8 kHz pulse. If one of the devices on the network does not employ this standard, then real-time traffic could be potentially delayed, causing jitter in the output.

## AVB Hardware
- AVB Talkers. These devices act as the source for an AVB stream, sending out audio onto the network.
- AVB Listeners. These devices are the destinations for the streams sent out by the Talkers.
- AVB Switches. This is the network hub to which every Talker and Listener must be connected. At its most basic level, an AVB Switch analyzes and prioritizes traffic on the network.
- AVB Controllers. A controller can be a talker, a listener, or neither. These devices handle routing, clock, and other settings for AVB devices using AVDECC.

## Network Structure

AVB on a 100Mbit network can handle up to 7 switch hops.  It is typically required to create a combination of star and leaf designs for a show network.

```diagram

```




### Redundancy

Redundancy within an AVB system is a completely separate infrastructure of switches, as AVB can only be enabled in 1 VLAN per switch.



### Adamson CS Series Connection
> ADAMSON redundancy through 1 cable uses 2 pairs of copper within the same cable for the 2 networks.  As such, it reduces bandwidth from 1Gbit to 100Mbit per network.
{.is-warning}




## AVB Streams
AVB will package the audio data into a stream, with each stream containing 8 channels, plus clocking data.  This improves efficiency of the network.

# AUVITRAN

```diagram

```




Agora H1 network endpoint in combination with Auvitrans AVB card is an easy to use Dante to AVB converter (although it can also function as a Dante to Other converter too).

The AVB Card offered by Auvitran does not feature Redundancy.  Other options are currently being researched for redundancy.

Two softwares are required to operate Auvitran, and they are windows only (Parallels compatible).

## AVS Control Panel
AVS Control Panel runs the background services to ensure the main software runs well.  

![auvitran_control_panel.png](/engineering/avb/auvitran_control_panel.png =500x){.align-center}


> Ensure that the services are operational and on the correct network before proceeding.
{.is-success}


## AVS Monitor

AVS monitor is the main control and monitoring software that the user interacts with.  Once connected correctly, the below view should be available with an overview of the hardware.

![auvitran_1.png](/engineering/avb/auvitran_1.png){.align-center}

> 1. Check Clock Settings: usually the mixer will be the master clock, and thus we sync through Dante.  Note that the CS series boxes will only work at 96kHz.
> 2. Check if signal is being received through Dante.  If not, check dante patching.
> 3. If signal is recieved but not forwarded to the output, check the matrix.
{.is-info}

# HIVE

> Latest download links @
> https://github.com/christophe-calmejane/Hive/releases
{.is-warning}

AVB Patching software from various companies can typically only patch products from that company, even if they aree AVB Milan Certified.

HIVE replaces Dante Controller as an open source, free patching software for any AVB device.

## Preferences


- Tick "Show Talkers on Top" in order to keeep the same layout as Dante Controller
- Protocol is typically Pcap, and you can tick whether or not it will communicate over Wi-Fi.
![hive_preferences.png](/engineering/avb/hive_preferences.png =300x){.align-center}

## Stream Based View

- The stream view shows the connections of the STREAM to the boxes, NOT the channels.  For example the Agora H1 has 2 streams of AVB available at 96kHz.  
- This view is used to delete the old patch, for example a stream that is no longer online.
![hive_stream_view.png](/engineering/avb/hive_stream_view.png =500x){.align-center}

## Channel Based View

- The channel view is the main view used for patching individual channels to cabinets.
- The color code is useful to see when a channel patch is working correctly.  It should be a green circle.
- Can be patched just like dante, just click on the intersection.

![hive_channel_view.png](/engineering/avb/hive_channel_view.png =500x){.align-center}

## Possible Problems

> HIVE has good troubleshooting tips for each error within the program.  Just click on the color code and hover over each color.
![hive_troubleshooting.png](/engineering/avb/hive_troubleshooting.png =500x) {.align-center}
{.is-info}
